messages.subject: multiple plots/pdf without looping
parts:
Hi there,

Consider the following code example:

> library(ggplot2)
> plot<-ggplot(mtcars)+geom_point(aes(x=cyl,y=mpg))+facet_grid(vs ~ gear)
> pdf("myPlot.pdf")
> plot
> dev.off()

gives me 1 pdf with mpg plotted over cyl for each combination of vs and gear (don't ask me why I chose these four variable ... haha ). I would like to use a 5th variable to generate plots for lets say each carb. That should give me plots for carb=1,2,3,4,6 and 8. How should I do that? Is there something like:

> plot<-ggplot(mtcars)+geom_point(aes(x=cyl,y=mpg))+facet_grid(vs ~ gear)+multiple_pages(carb)

Many thanks in advance for any kind of help :-)

Irsan

messages.author: 56148d40b6509fff
messages.subject: Re: multiple plots/pdf without looping
parts:
Irsan,

Here's one suggestion -- use dlply() from the plyr package. dlply()
breaks a dataframe into pieces, applies a function to each piece, and
returns a list. Please see simple example below.

Dave
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
require(plyr)
require(ggplot2)

plot.fn = function(df) {
tstring = paste('Plot of vs =', df$vs[1])
qplot(x=cyl,y=mpg, data=df, main=tstring) + facet_wrap('gear')
}

myplots = dlply(mtcars, ~vs, plot.fn)
typeof(myplots)
print(myplots)
